name: Jade Reyes

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What does your workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and a junior operator feeding corrugated board into a box die cutter. I left school after secondary school and am still learning which die fits which order; the lead checks my setup. I like watching a clean box fold, but damp board jams the press and sends agency workers home early.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home life like, and do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner books transport and answers families' messages in a school office. We have two school-age children and a mortgage. I earn a lower factory rate, we have about two weeks of expenses saved, and there are few similar jobs nearby. I use AI now and then to draft a jam note, then check the machine number myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the box line that a tidier dispatch list would help, but somebody still has to catch a crooked cut on the cardboard press. My worry is whether we get full shifts, not whether a screen can write a list.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The die cutter stops when damp board jams it, and the agency sends us home early some weeks. I earn the junior rate and we have about two weeks of bills saved against the mortgage. A quiet AI story doesn't fix a lost shift, and there are few other factories nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep feeding and checking boxes while my lead checks my die settings. I'll ask the supervisor for the next month's shift board before we book school costs. I use AI now and then to make a clear note about a jam, but I'll check the machine number first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the ordinary rota, even if AI stays small. I can manage one short week; two in a row make the mortgage tight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened after the damp pallet?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last month a damp pallet stopped the cutter for half a shift. My partner's school-office pay covered groceries, but we delayed the children's winter shoes until the next wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make your shifts steadier?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I want to learn a proper changeover from the lead so I can take more regular shifts. I wouldn't call an occasional AI note a new skill or an answer to our bills.

say: **Dispatch lists** can improve while the cardboard die still needs a person checking cuts.
Our **shift board** matters more to the mortgage than small AI gains.
think: Two weeks of **savings** cannot cover several shortened factory shifts.
Few **nearby plants** leave me little room to replace the junior wage.
do: **Keep** feeding and checking cardboard boxes under the lead operator.
**Ask** for the next month shift board before paying school costs.
feel: **Anxious** about current rota losses despite modest AI change.
S0.quote: I can manage one short week; two in a row make the mortgage tight.
fieldNote: Her **baseline risk** is irregular junior paid hours when damp board stops the die cutter.
The existing **occasional AI note** is not tagged new learning; a thin reserve keeps her anxious.

steps.text: Keep feeding cardboard die cutter and checking box cuts
Ask supervisor for next month of paid shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the union meeting that AI booking work could hit my partner's school office before robots stack our boxes. The factory should give us paid time to check any new production plan and tell people when rosters change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner books school transport and answers parent emails; those are exactly the tasks on the card. If those hours shrink while my agency shifts are uneven, two weeks of savings will go quickly. I'd be open to a proven machine screen if somebody shows me the safe way.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the union steward to request paid training slots and a written rota notice. If the factory offers a paid supervised lesson on its new die-cutting screen, I'll attend and practise changing a job order with the machine stopped. At home we'll list the mortgage and children's costs against one wage before agreeing to any extra spending.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about two wages being exposed, though I can take practical steps. I don't want to discover an office cut from a missing pay packet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your partner ask at work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner would ask their school office manager which transport bookings are moving to software and whether paid hours will change. We can then plan from a written rota, not a rumour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the supervised lesson cover?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I want the instructor to show the stop button, the correct die number and the first-box check. A paid lesson on an idle press is safer than learning during a live run.

say: **School bookings** may change before robots take physical box stacking.
The **union steward** should seek paid instruction and written rota notice.
think: My partner's **office hours** and my own agency shifts could both shrink.
A **proven machine screen** is worth learning if the lesson is paid and safe.
do: **Ask** union steward for paid instruction and written rota notice.
**Attend** supervised screen lesson if a paid place is offered.
**Review** mortgage and school costs against one wage.
feel: **Anxious** about a realistic reduction in household paid hours.
S1.quote: I don't want to discover an office cut from a missing pay packet.
fieldNote: The **household risk** includes a partner whose booking and email work fits the card.
Her **screen learning** requires a real paid lesson on a stopped press, consistent with steady adaptability.

steps.text: Ask union steward for paid screen lesson and written rota notice
Learn die-cutting screen if supervised paid lesson offered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AI by 2028 could handle my partner's school bookings, then capable robots around 2031 could feed and stack our boxes. I'd tell the union that a family can't wait three years for help while one wage disappears sooner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my partner's office hours to be cut sharply by 2028, and a robot could take the junior press tasks I still struggle to do fast. With two weeks saved, I lie awake working out which mortgage payment we could cover. Few local plants will be hiring the same low-skill work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll ask the school and factory for written hours plans, and take the mortgage numbers to a household advice office if a cut is confirmed. I'll apply to posted local stockroom or production jobs with enough hours and pay to cover our bills if either wage falls. If the factory offers a real funded, paid-time safe die-setting course, I'll enrol; I won't buy a certificate on credit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I expect a big loss of household pay, and the mortgage is the part I cannot put off.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which costs would go first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would cancel the planned weekend trip and stop the children's paid after-school club only if shifts actually fall. We would keep food and the mortgage first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a training place real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The course has to include a guarded changeover and a lead operator watching me set the die. A brochure about future factory roles is no place on a training rota.

say: **2028 thinking AI** could cut school booking hours before robots reach the box line around 2031.
The **union** should demand written plans and income support before wages disappear.
think: A large **household wage cut** is likely, with only two weeks saved.
Few **local jobs** make replacing the junior press wage difficult.
do: **Seek** written school and factory hours plans; take mortgage figures to household advice if a cut is confirmed.
**Apply** for posted local work if either wage falls and pay covers bills.
**Enrol** in guarded die-setting course if funded paid place offered.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected major wage loss and sleepless mortgage worry.
S2.quote: A brochure about future factory roles is no place on a training rota.
fieldNote: She expects **school-office cuts in 2028**, before capable physical robots around 2031.
An actual **application** needs a posted local job at adequate hours and pay; training needs funded paid practice.

steps.text: Take mortgage figures to household advice office if school or factory hours cut confirmed
Apply if either wage falls to posted local stockroom/production job with bill-covering regular hours/pay
Enrol in die-setting course if offered funded paid guarded place
Cancel weekend trip if household paid hours fall

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If thinking AI arrives in 2031 and capable box-handling robots around 2034, I'd tell the union we have a few years to get paid training places and clear notice. The school office could still lose booking work before our press loses people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 48 when the office work changes and 51 when robots can run hands-on tasks. My partner and I still owe most of the mortgage, and two weeks saved will not grow by wishing. We could make a plan if paid shifts continue long enough.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep the paid box shifts and set aside a small new amount from each full pay packet, after mortgage and food. If the factory offers a funded die-setting certificate with paid release and guarded practice, I'll enrol this year. After qualifying, if press shifts fall, I'll apply to posted local setter jobs only if their regular hours and pay cover our household bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the future household pay, but less cornered than in the fast case. I can learn at work without leaving the wage first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you build a reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our first savings target is one month of mortgage, food and travel costs. I would transfer money only after a full paid week, not claim the two weeks already saved are new money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What must a die-setting course include?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want to set the die on an idle guarded press, produce a test box and have the lead check its fold. If the course only shows videos, it won't qualify me for a setter posting.

say: **2031 thinking AI** affects school bookings before robots handle boxes around 2034.
The **union** should seek paid training and clear change notice.
think: At **48**, the school-office wage may shrink while the mortgage remains.
A **paid certificate** and real setter posting could protect income if press hours fall.
do: **Keep** paid box shifts and save new money after full weeks.
**Enrol** in funded die-setting certificate if paid guarded place offered.
**Apply** to posted local setter role after qualifying if hours fall and pay suffices.
feel: **Anxious** about household pay, with more time to prepare.
S3.quote: I can learn at work without leaving the wage first.
fieldNote: New **saving** comes from future full pay packets, not existing cash.
Training and a later **setter application** both keep their actual funding, qualification, vacancy and pay conditions.

steps.text: Save new money from full box-line wages after essential bills
Enrol in funded die-setting certificate if paid guarded place offered
Apply if qualified and shifts cut to posted local setter role with bill-covering regular hours/pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AI in 2036 could take school booking tasks and capable robots around 2039 could run box lines. I'd tell our union not to wait until a robot arrives to ask how families will keep their wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 when thinking AI arrives and 56 when robots handle the physical press work. We still need paid work then, and our mortgage will not vanish just because there is a decade's warning. The current two-week cushion and uneven hours keep me careful now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep the factory shifts and try to put fresh money from every full week into a reserve. I'll take an offered funded die-setting course only with paid time and safe practical work. Each year we'll check actual local vacancies; if either wage falls after 2036, I'll apply to posted local setter or stockroom jobs I qualify for only where regular pay and hours cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the thin reserve and today's uneven shifts, even with a longer runway. The decade before thinking AI in 2036 can help us build a cushion if the wages actually arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would one month of savings cover?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would first aim for one full month of mortgage, food and travel in cash. If a week is cut short, we cannot pretend the planned deposit happened.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the union bargain for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the union to bargain for paid release and a written notice before line changes. The classroom seat has to be offered and the practice press guarded; a promise at a meeting won't pay the mortgage.

say: **2036 thinking AI** may cut school bookings before robots run the box line around 2039.
The **union** should secure paid release and notice before roster changes.
think: At **56**, I expect to need paid work beyond robot arrival.
A **thin reserve** and uneven shifts matter even with ten years to prepare.
do: **Continue** paid factory shifts and build a real new reserve.
**Attend** funded guarded die-setting course if a paid place opens.
**Apply** for qualified posted local work if household wages fall and pay suffices.
feel: **Anxious** about current thin savings and irregular paid shifts.
S4.quote: The decade before thinking AI in 2036 can help us build a cushion if the wages actually arrive.
fieldNote: She does not confuse a **decade of warning** with guaranteed paid shifts or saving.
Her **training and local applications** stay conditional on offered paid practice, qualifications, reduced wages and sufficient pay.

steps.text: Save new money from each full paid box-line week
Seek paid release and roster notice through factory union
Attend die-setting course if offered funded paid guarded place
Apply for posted local qualified job if wages fall, pay sufficient

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which worries you most, and what would help?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The 2028 case worries me most because my partner's school-office hours could shrink before robots reach my box press around 2031. A written hours plan, a real funded paid training place and a posted local job with bill-covering pay would help us keep the mortgage current.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask how a family pays the mortgage while both adults are being told to retrain. A cardboard box can wait for a new die; our mortgage payment cannot wait for a promised course.

headlineQuote: A cardboard box can wait for a new die; our mortgage payment cannot wait for a promised course.
portrait: **Jade**, 43, is a junior cardboard die-cutter operator with secondary school education and a lower factory wage.
She and her school-office partner support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with only two weeks of expenses saved.
She uses **AI occasionally** for jam notes and waits for proven paid instruction before learning a new machine screen.
Uneven shifts keep her **anxious** even in AI Plateau; fast AGI alarms her because both wages could fall.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut her partner’s school-office hours before robots threaten box-press shifts around 2031.
whatWouldHelp: A **written hours plan**, offered paid guarded training and a posted local job at bill-covering pay would help.
